This no longer matches the code behavior.; Why it fails: Operators reading the README will have incorrect mental model of resource usage and cancellation timing during retriggers.; ### Issue 2: agents.md documentation outdated

      Problem: Lines: 307-309; The README contains documentation about the autofix retrigger dedup feature that still describes the old behavior with `cancel-in-progress: true`. It states "the loser is killed mid-flight after it has already spent runner minutes and possibly LLM setup tokens."; After this PR, the workflow uses `cancel-in-progress: false`, where the losing run is cancelled while still pending (before consuming runner minutes), and only the redundant queued run appears in the Actions UI.; Why it matters at runtime: Operators reading the README will have an incorrect mental model of resource usage and cancellation timing during retriggers, potentially leading to misdiagnosis of waste or unexpected behavior.; ### Verification of Functional Changes; I verified the code changes in the modified files:; **1. `.github/workflows/review_autofix.yml` (line 212)**; - Changed from `cancel-in-progress: true` to `cancel-in-progress: false`; - Added comprehensive comments explaining the new behavior; - Syntax is valid YAML and GitHub Actions schema; **2. `scripts/gh_gh_helpers.sh` (line ~1064-1072)**; - Updated documentation comments to reflect the new behavior; - Accurately describes: "the loser is cancelled while pending, but the redundant queued run still surfaces in the Actions UI and consumes a workflow_dispatch API call"; **3. Consistency with repository patterns**; Other workflows in the repo already use `cancel-in-progress: false`:; - orchestrate_poll.yml; - orchestrate.yml; - implement.yml; - workflow-log-analysis.yml; - comprehensive-test-and-release.yml; ### Assessment; **Functional correctness**: The implementation is correct. The concurrency change and updated inline comments accurately reflect the new behavior.; **Documentation gap**: The README.md still contains outdated documentation that should be updated to match the new behavior described in the code comments.; ### Recommended Action; Update README.md lines 307-309 to reflect the new `cancel-in-progress: false` behavior:; - Replace "the loser is killed mid-flight after it has already spent runner minutes" with description of pending cancellation behavior; - Note that redundant queued runs are auto-cancelled by GitHub while pending; HARDENING_ISSUE_FOUND: YES; The documentation inconsistency should be addressed to maintain operational clarity and ensure that future maintainers have an accurate understanding of the system's behavior.

Specifically: "both land in `pr-autofix-${PR}` with `cancel-in-progress: true`) and the loser was killed 4–10 s after start, burning runner minutes". AI agents using these instructions may plan or reason about the system based on obsolete semantics.; Why it fails: AI agents (including future Codex runs) could draw incorrect conclusions about retrigger efficiency, concurrency collisions, and failure modes when analyzing or modifying related workflows.; ## ANALYSIS OF PEER CHECK LOGIC (PASS 1 CONCERNS); The concerns raised by pass 1 reviewers about the `autofix_retrigger_has_inflight_peer` function have been evaluated:; **Current behavior is CORRECT for `cancel-in-progress: false`:**; - With `cancel-in-progress: false`, GitHub automatically collapses queued runs to only the most recent one; - If Run A is in_progress and pushes 2, 3, 4 happen rapidly, GitHub cancels the intermediate queued runs and keeps only the newest queued run; - The peer check prevents unnecessary dispatches when a synchronize-triggered run is already pending or running; - The 180-minute timeout provides an upper bound on execution time; The concern about "reviewing stale commits" is addressed by GitHub's concurrency semantics - the queued run always represents the latest commit at the time it entered the queue.; ## VERDICT; **Code changes are correct and complete.** The concurrency strategy change from `cancel-in-progress: true` to `cancel-in-progress: false` is properly implemented in:; - `.github/workflows/review_autofix.yml` (concurrency configuration + comments); - `scripts/gh_helpers.sh` (documentation comments); **Documentation alignment is needed** in:; - `README.md` line ~307 (Autofix retrigger dedup section); - `agents.md` section 20 (Autofix Retrigger Dedup); Both documentation files still describe the OLD behavior (`cancel-in-progress: true`) which misrepresents the current implementation.; NO_CHANGES_REQUIRED_IN_CODE; Documentation updates needed in README.md and agents.md to align with the new `cancel-in-progress: false` behavior.

  [7] File: agents.md, line 440 (line ~440)
      Problem: The instruction file states "both land in `pr-autofix-${PR}` with `cancel-in-progress: true`… and the loser was killed 4–10 s after start, burning runner minutes…" This no longer matches the repository's configured behavior. Future Codex runs that consult these agent instructions may reason incorrectly about retrigger efficiency, collision handling, and failure modes.; AI agents planning or modifying related workflows could draw incorrect conclusions.; === HARDENING REVIEW ===; A hardening suggestion was raised by a cross-pollination reviewer: "Modify the gh api filter to also check if any in_flight peer is already processing the current GITHUB_SHA. If not, do not skip."; Assessment: This suggestion is **not implemented**. The current "skip if any peer exists" design is sound given GitHub Actions' concurrency semantics with `cancel-in-progress: false`:; - When multiple pushes occur, only the newest queued run survives; older queued runs are auto-cancelled before start.; - Consequently, if apeer run exists on the branch, it either targets the current HEAD (same as the retrigger intent) or a newer HEAD (in which case it supersedes any older work).; - Adding SHA filtering would risk skipping dispatch when the peer is on an older SHA that somehow remained queued, but that state is impossible under GitHub's documented behavior: older queued jobs are always cancelled when a newer one arrives.; - The additional check would require either an extra API call or larger response parsing, increase complexity, and could degrade dedup effectiveness by causing more dispatches, increasing waste rather than reducing it.; - The helper already "fails open" on any API error; a SHA check would introduce a new failure mode that could block dispatch incorrectly if SHA comparison failed.; Therefore this suggestion is classified: **ignored — unnecessary complexity that would likely degrade the dedup's resource-saving goal**.; === ACTIONS TAKEN ===; Applied documentation patches to align docs with code:; 1. README.md; - Lines 307-309 (3 lines) updated.; - Changed `cancel-in-progress: true` → `false` and replaced "loser is killed mid-flight after it has already spent runner minutes and possibly LLM setup tokens." with "so the loser is cancelled while pending — but the redundant queued run still appears in the Actions UI and consumes a `workflow_dispatch` API call."; - Result: Section now matches workflow comment and actual behavior.; 2. agents.md; - Line 440 (single paragraph) updated.; - Changed `cancel-in-progress: true` → `false` and replaced the clause describing the loser burning runner minutes with "and the losing run is cancelled while pending — but the redundant queued run would still appear in the Actions UI and consume a `workflow_dispatch` API call."; - Result: Operational instructions now reflect the new concurrency semantics.; Both changes are minimal, preserve existing structure, and keep all other content intact.; === VERIFICATION ===; - Confirmed `.github/workflows/review_autofix.yml` contains `cancel-in-progress: false` (line ~212) with correct explanatory comments.; - Confirmed `scripts/gh_helpers.sh` comment around autofix_retrigger_has_inflight_peer reflects `cancel-in-progress: false` behavior.; - Verified no remaining `cancel-in-progress: true` references in the autofix retrigger documentation (README.md, agents.md) after patch.; - Checked that the "Both entry points land in the same..." lead-in sentence remains intact; context preserved.; - Searched other tracked files: no further outdated references affecting this PR scope.; === ASSUMPTIONS ===; None beyond what is evident in code and PR description. The documentation updates are clearly required, and the code logic does not require additional SHA-based peer filtering.; === MISSING CONTEXT ===; === SUMMARY ===; The PR's concurrency change is correctly implemented. The only outstanding issues were documentation omissions, now fixed. No logic bugs found. No further action required.; Files changed (this review's edits):; - README.md:307-309; - agents.md:440
